# Unfolded Wasn’t Ready: Webb’s Road to Science Operations

Webb was designed to fold into the Ariane 5 fairing because its operational configuration was too large for the available rocket. Deploying the telescope involved more than 50 major steps and over 300 possible single points of failure. Any one could have diminished or crippled the mission, and repair was not possible at Webb’s distance from Earth.

By the second week, the secondary mirror and both primary-mirror wings had unfolded and latched, completing Webb’s fully deployed operational configuration. But deployment was only part of the process. During the first month, the telescope and its instruments cooled for several weeks.

Mirror alignment took place in months two through four. Instrument-mode calibration followed in months five and six. Webb began routine science operations after six months.
